title: Regular Expression Denial of Service and Resource Exhaustion Static Analysis Rules

rules.name: Regular expression with catastrophic backtracking
rules.description: A regular expression is compiled or used with nested quantifiers such as (a+)+, (.*)+ or ([a-zA-Z]+)*. On a failing match the engine tries exponentially many ways to split the input, so a short attacker-supplied string can pin a worker for minutes or hours. The regex engine also backtracks across alternations that overlap.
rules.remediation_example: pattern = re.compile(r'(?:a+)+\Z')  # replace with a linear pattern, or use the third-party 'regex' module with timeout=

rules.name: Outbound HTTP request without a timeout
rules.description: A requests or httpx call omits the timeout= parameter. The client will then wait indefinitely for the peer, so one slow or hostile endpoint exhausts the worker pool and stalls the whole service. Every outbound request needs a bounded timeout.
